text:
A: Hi! Can you hear me? Sorry, my internet's been a bit funny all day.
B: Yes, I can hear you fine. Abena.
A: I'm Sana. Nice to meet you. This is my last one, I think? Erm, is it yours too?
B: Fourth one, yes. I think that's everyone.
A: I'm kind of sad, actually, I was dreading it but it's been nice. Where are you?
B: Crawley. Near Gatwick. Before you say it, yes, the planes, and no, I don't hear them anymore.
A: Lol, okay, I won't say it. I'm in Luton, so we've got an airport as well. Everyone just thinks of the airport.
B: Exactly. That's all anyone knows about Luton and Crawley. Airports and traffic.
A: And the Arndale, lol. So what do you do?
B: Pharmacy technician. Three days a week, dispensing, checking scripts. You?
A: Erm, I'm job-hunting at the minute. I was at a nursery but it closed down five months ago, so I'm applying for nursery jobs, teaching assistant, that kind of thing.
B: That's annoying, when it's not your fault. Have you got your paediatric first aid up to date? Because schools always ask for that first.
A: Oh my god, no, it needs renewing. I keep meaning to.
B: Do it this week. It's one day, and it puts you at the top of the pile. My son's school, every TA they hire, first thing they ask.
A: Okay, yeah, that's actually really helpful, thank you. You've got kids?
B: Two. Thirteen and nine. The thirteen-year-old is attached to his PlayStation. The nine-year-old I can still bribe.
A: Nine's a nice age. I'd love kids soon, but, you know, money and that.
B: Money is always the thing. You'll manage, though, you clearly know what you're doing with children.
A: Aww. Erm, can I say, your braids are really nice. Do you do them yourself?
B: Yes, mine and my daughter's. Takes forever. I put a film on and just go.
A: That's me with mehndi. I do henna for weddings, brides and that, and a bride's hands can be like four hours, so I just put a drama on in the background.
B: Four hours, okay, so you understand. People think it's nothing. It's not nothing, your back is finished afterwards.
A: Yes! My shoulders are always shattered after. What do you watch while you're doing it?
B: Ghanaian films on YouTube, Nollywood, whatever. Or the crime thing everyone's talking about on Netflix. I half watch, honestly. I'm scrolling Vinted at the same time.
A: I do that with Pakistani dramas with my mum, but I get way too invested. There's one now where the mother-in-law is pure evil, like, she's hiding the daughter-in-law's letters and everything, and my mum is shouting at the telly.
B: The mother-in-law is always evil. It's the same in the Nollywood ones. If there's a mother-in-law, you know she's going to poison someone by the end.
A: Lol, exactly! It's like, the rule.
B: Your family's from Pakistan, then?
A: Yeah, Mirpur. I came here when I was nine. I've been back twice, but I get so anxious flying, like, the whole time I'm just thinking about everything going wrong.
B: I fly to Ghana every couple of years and the flying is fine, it's the price that gives me the anxiety. Christmas flights, it's criminal.
A: That's so true. We went for my cousin's wedding and my dad was
